note: Ordered technique chains distilled from public advisories. Each step's `alternatives` are the documented variants of that stage (a playbook branch: LockBit enters by exploit OR stolen credentials), matched as any-of. A chain is the COMMON path, not a required one — real intrusions skip, repeat and reorder steps, which is why matching is a fuzzy subsequence rather than an equality test.

playbooks.name: Conti
playbooks.description: Conti ransomware affiliate playbook: spearphish entry, hands-on-keyboard PowerShell/Cobalt Strike, LSASS credential dumping, SMB/PsExec lateral movement, and mass encryption.

playbooks.name: LockBit
playbooks.description: LockBit affiliate playbook: initial access via an exploited public-facing app or stolen RDP credentials, tooling staged on the host, Cobalt Strike beaconing, credential theft, lateral spread, and double-extortion exfiltration before encryption.

playbooks.name: BlackCat (ALPHV)
playbooks.description: BlackCat/ALPHV playbook: identity-driven access with compromised VPN/RDP credentials, hands-on-keyboard scripting, privileged credential theft, deployment via PsExec/SMB, and cross-platform Rust encryption after staged exfiltration.

playbooks.name: Akira
playbooks.description: Akira ransomware playbook: VPN access without MFA, credential theft with LSASS tooling, Active Directory discovery, RDP/SMB lateral movement, WinRAR staging with rclone/FileZilla exfiltration, shadow-copy deletion, then encryption.

playbooks.name: Scattered Spider
playbooks.description: Scattered Spider playbook: social-engineered help-desk resets and vishing rather than malware for entry, MFA fatigue or SIM-swap to finish the logon, legitimate remote-access tooling instead of implants, credentials pulled from password stores, SaaS/cloud discovery, cloud exfiltration, and ransomware deployment last.

playbooks.name: Black Basta
playbooks.description: Black Basta playbook: phishing (historically QakBot) for entry, user execution of the dropped loader, Mimikatz-style credential theft, exploitation for privilege escalation, RDP/PsExec lateral movement, RClone exfiltration, shadow-copy deletion, then encryption.

playbooks.name: BlackSuit (Royal)
playbooks.description: BlackSuit/Royal playbook: phishing or an exploited public-facing service for entry, tooling staged and beaconing over HTTP(S), credential theft, RDP lateral movement, exfiltration over alternative protocols, shadow-copy deletion, then encryption.

playbooks.name: Play
playbooks.description: Play ransomware playbook: valid accounts or an exploited public-facing service (FortiOS, Exchange) for entry, security tooling disabled, credential theft, Active Directory discovery, SMB/RDP lateral movement, WinRAR staging with WinSCP exfiltration, then encryption.
